help.intro: A text of about 200 words about the two brothers who collected the fairy tales the whole world knows: Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm. They did not invent Hansel and Gretel or Little Red Riding Hood; they wrote down what people told them, published the first book in 1812, and the final edition of 1857 has 200 tales translated into more than 160 languages. The text also tells which woman told them the most stories, why the first edition was not for children, and where the German Fairy Tale Route runs. All facts are real and were checked. You read it in the Präteritum, the tense of fairy tales and written stories (sie lebten, sie sammelten, sie schrieben, es war einmal), and with your first relative clauses (die Frau, die ihnen die Märchen erzählte; das Buch, das 1812 erschien). Read for the story first, then find one name, number or place per question.
help.tips[0].title: Präteritum: the tense of written stories
help.tips[0].text: Regular verbs: stem + -te: sie lebten, sie sammelten, sie arbeiteten, er erzählte, sie wohnte. Irregular verbs change the vowel: schreiben → schrieb, kommen → kam, gehen → ging, geben → gab, finden → fand, sterben → starb, erscheinen → erschien. The most common: war, hatte, wurde, gab (es gab), konnte, musste, wollte. Every fairy tale begins with Es war einmal (once upon a time) and ends with Und wenn sie nicht gestorben sind, dann leben sie noch heute.
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: The brothers lived in Kassel, collected fairy tales and wrote them down.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: The first book appeared in 1812 and had 86 tales.
help.tips[0].check.why: schreiben is irregular: schrieb. geschrieben is the participle.
help.tips[1].title: Relative clauses: der, die, das
help.tips[1].text: A relative clause gives more information about a noun; it starts with der, die or das (like the article) and puts the verb at the end: die Frau, die ihnen Märchen erzählte; das Buch, das 1812 erschien; der Bruder, der die Sprache erforschte. Accusative: den for masculine: der Wolf, den der Jäger fand. Plural: die: die Märchen, die alle kennen. Commas before and after the clause.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: Dorothea Viehmann was the woman who told the brothers the most tales.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: The Fairy Tale Route is a road that leads from Hanau to Bremen.
help.tips[1].check.why: das Buch is neuter, so the relative pronoun is das.
help.remember[0]: Präteritum: lebte, sammelte (regular); schrieb, kam, gab, erschien (irregular); Es war einmal.
help.remember[1]: Relative clause: die Frau, die …; das Buch, das …; der Wolf, den …; verb at the end.
help.exam: Short texts about famous people and books, written in the Präteritum, are a typical reading task at this level.
help.hook: Two brothers, one old woman with a basket of stories, and a book translated into 160 languages: read how Hansel, Gretel and Little Red Riding Hood were written down.
help.vocab[6].example: Die Brüder Grimm haben die Märchen gesammelt.
passageTranslation:
Hansel and Gretel, Little Red Riding Hood, Snow White, Cinderella: every child in the world knows these fairy tales. But who wrote them? Nobody. The brothers Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm collected them.

Jacob was born in Hanau in 1785, Wilhelm in 1786. As young men they lived in Kassel and worked in a library. They were interested in the old German language. That is why they collected stories that people had been telling for a hundred years but never wrote down. The brothers did not go through the villages. People came to them. The most important was Dorothea Viehmann, a woman who sold vegetables at the market in Kassel. She told them over forty tales.

The first book appeared in 1812 and was called 'Children's and Household Tales'. It had 86 tales and was not for children: the stories were often cruel, and the book had long footnotes. Wilhelm changed the texts in the following years. He made them shorter, more beautiful and less brutal. The last edition appeared in 1857 and had 200 tales.

Today the tales exist in more than 160 languages. Only the Bible is translated into more languages. Since 2005 the books belong to UNESCO's Memory of the World.

Whoever wants to see the places drives the German Fairy Tale Route: 600 kilometres from Hanau to Bremen, where the Town Musicians of Bremen stand as a statue. And in Kassel there is a museum called Grimmwelt.

questions[0].explanation: "Aber wer hat sie geschrieben? Niemand. Die Brüder Jacob und Wilhelm Grimm haben sie gesammelt."
questions[0].optionsTranslation[2]: Nobody; the Brothers Grimm collected the tales.
questions[0].optionsTranslation[3]: Dorothea Viehmann, the woman from the market in Kassel, wrote them.
questions[1].explanation: lebten, arbeiteten = Präteritum of regular verbs (leben, arbeiten) with -te and the plural ending -n.
questions[1].questionTranslation: 'As young men they lived in Kassel and worked in a library.' Which tense is that?
questions[1].optionsTranslation[2]: perfect with haben and sein, like haben gelebt
questions[2].options[2]: Sie haben alte Bücher aus der Bibliothek in Kassel kopiert.
questions[2].explanation: "Die Brüder gingen nicht durch die Dörfer. Die Menschen kamen zu ihnen."
questions[2].questionTranslation: How did the brothers collect the tales?
questions[2].optionsTranslation[1]: People came to them and told stories.
questions[2].optionsTranslation[2]: They copied old books from the library in Kassel.
questions[3].explanation: die starts the relative clause about die Frau; the verb verkaufte stands at the end.
questions[3].questionTranslation: 'Dorothea Viehmann, a woman who sold vegetables at the market in Kassel.' What is die?
questions[3].optionsTranslation[1]: a relative pronoun; it starts the relative clause
questions[3].optionsTranslation[3]: a personal pronoun for she, so for Dorothea Viehmann herself
questions[4].explanation: "Es hatte 86 Märchen und war nicht für Kinder: Die Geschichten waren oft grausam, und das Buch hatte lange Fußnoten."
questions[4].questionTranslation: Why was the first book not for children?
questions[4].optionsTranslation[1]: because the stories were often cruel and the book had long footnotes
questions[4].optionsTranslation[2]: because it had only 86 pages and the children wanted to read more
questions[5].options[0]: Er machte sie länger und brutaler.
questions[5].options[1]: Er machte sie kürzer, schöner und weniger brutal.
questions[5].options[2]: Er übersetzte sie ins Englische und verkaufte sie in London.
questions[5].options[3]: Er verkaufte sie auf dem Markt.
questions[5].explanation: "Wilhelm änderte die Texte in den nächsten Jahren. Er machte sie kürzer, schöner und weniger brutal."
questions[5].questionTranslation: What did Wilhelm do with the texts?
questions[5].optionsTranslation[0]: He made them longer and more brutal.
questions[5].optionsTranslation[1]: He made them shorter, more beautiful and less brutal.
questions[5].optionsTranslation[2]: He translated them into English and sold them in London.
questions[5].optionsTranslation[3]: He sold them at the market.
questions[6].explanation: "Heute gibt es die Märchen in mehr als 160 Sprachen. Nur die Bibel ist in mehr Sprachen übersetzt."
questions[6].questionTranslation: Into how many languages are the tales translated?
questions[6].optionsTranslation[2]: into 200, as many as the tales
questions[7].explanation: "… fährt die Deutsche Märchenstraße: 600 Kilometer von Hanau bis Bremen …"
questions[7].questionTranslation: What is the German Fairy Tale Route?
questions[7].optionsTranslation[1]: a route of 600 kilometres from Hanau to Bremen
questions[7].optionsTranslation[2]: a big museum in Hanau with all the tales of the Brothers Grimm
questions[0].options[3]: Dorothea Viehmann, die Frau vom Markt in Kassel, hat sie geschrieben.
